meta.purpose: Static JSON:API response for an Ember frontend rendering the current Albany Commercial Rent Stabilization bill as a source-coded provenance article.
meta.canonicalCurrentTextSource: NYS Assembly A5568A official bill PDF / NYSenate bill page
caveats: The current bill text nodes are drawn from the A5568A/S8319 source-map article and cross-checked against the official A5568A text layer used in the project.
Provenance marks are review metadata derived from the semantic HTML source map; they are not a final legal opinion.
reviewStatus=counsel-reviewed means substantially carried through the Fair Rent NYC 2022 counsel-redline lineage, not an independent guarantee of legal sufficiency.
Any future public legal claim should be reviewed against the official source documents and counsel memos.
meta.baseRationale: e.json kept the cleanest Ember-ready contract: current Albany bill as readable text-nodes plus range-based text-marks, omissions, source-notes, crosswalks, and city-draft suggestions.

appliedEdits.edit: Added high-priority issue resources and made the chain-definition / renewal-rights risk lane explicit without changing the underlying bill text.
Added Ember component-tree guidance and style-class-rule resources while avoiding b.json's rendered-HTML-in-data coupling.
Added expanded body/view mode contract for legal-review and timeline filters.
Added the modeling principle that provenance should be represented as claims/marks against text units rather than presentation classes alone.
Kept exhaustive token-level models as optional audit-corpus pattern only; not used as the primary Ember route model.

meta.primaryModelWarning: This response is a frontend and legal-review workflow model. It is not legal advice. Provenance, reviewStatus, cityDraftStatus, and drafting-error flags should be verified by counsel before public reliance.
meta.auditCorpusPolicy: For the main Ember route, render text-nodes and compute segments from text-marks. Exhaustive token-fragment corpora such as h.json/i.json are better as secondary audit endpoints or developer tools, not the default reader payload.

attributes.title: Commercial Rent Stabilization — Albany Bill Source Map
attributes.description: One readable current Albany bill article with semantic provenance, review-status, omission, drafting-error, and city-intro-cue metadata.
attributes.modelingPrinciple: The current Albany bill remains the canonical readable article. Intro 93, Fair Rent NYC counsel redlines, Albany-only changes, omissions, review status, and city-intro recommendations are metadata attached to stable text nodes.
attributes.renderingModel: Render text-nodes in order as one article. For each node, build display spans by splitting node.text at text-mark boundaries. Render omissions and source-notes as callouts anchored to their target node. Use bodyClass view modes to change styling without mutating data.
attributes.provenancePolicy: Do not force uncertain language into a lineage category. When provenance is unclear or current Albany language differs materially from the reviewed lineage, mark it review-needed / needs-counsel.
renderingAlgorithm: 2. For each text-node, collect related text-marks and use start/end offsets to build non-overlapping display segments.
3. Compute segment classes from each covering mark: sourceLayer, sourceAction, reviewStatus, cityDraftStatus, topics, and kind.
4. Render omissions and source-notes anchored before, inside, or after the node according to anchorPosition / dataAttributes.
5. Apply visual emphasis by changing a view-mode body class, not by rewriting markup or data.

attributes.text: Section 1. Short title. This act shall be known and may be cited as the "New York city small business rent stabilization act".

attributes.text: § 2. Title 22 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new chapter 15 to read as follows:

attributes.label: COMMERCIAL RENT STABILIZATION
attributes.text: COMMERCIAL RENT STABILIZATION

attributes.label: § 22-1501 Application. This chapter applies to all leases and rental agreements for commercial spaces that are renewed,
attributes.text: § 22-1501 Application. This chapter applies to all leases and rental agreements for commercial spaces that are renewed, renegotiated, or entered into on or after July first, two thousand twenty-five.

attributes.label: § 22-1502 Definitions. As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the following meanings unless the context
attributes.text: § 22-1502 Definitions. As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the following meanings unless the context requires otherwise:

attributes.label: a. "Administering agency" shall mean any city agency, office, department, division, bureau or institution of government,
attributes.text: a. "Administering agency" shall mean any city agency, office, department, division, bureau or institution of government, the expenses of which are paid in whole or in part from the city treasury, as the mayor shall designate or establish to implement and enforce the provisions of this chapter.

attributes.label: b. "At-will tenant" shall mean a tenant, subtenant, lessee, sublessee, or any other persons lawfully entitled to use or
attributes.text: b. "At-will tenant" shall mean a tenant, subtenant, lessee, sublessee, or any other persons lawfully entitled to use or occupy any commercial premises without a written lease or other rental agreement, who has paid rent to a landlord for at least six months.

attributes.label: c. "Board" shall mean the commercial rent guidelines board established by subdivision a of section 22-1503 of this chapt
attributes.text: c. "Board" shall mean the commercial rent guidelines board established by subdivision a of section 22-1503 of this chapter.

attributes.label: d. "Chain business" shall mean an establishment that is part of a group of establishments that share a common landlord o
attributes.text: d. "Chain business" shall mean an establishment that is part of a group of establishments that share a common landlord or principal who owns at least thirty percent of each establishment where such establishments:

attributes.label: (1) engage in the same business; or
attributes.text: (1) engage in the same business; or

attributes.label: (2) operate pursuant to a franchise agreement with the same franchisor as defined in section six hundred eighty-one of t
attributes.text: (2) operate pursuant to a franchise agreement with the same franchisor as defined in section six hundred eighty-one of the general business law.

attributes.label: e. "Commercial space" shall mean a space used or occupied for non-residential purposes pursuant to a valid commercial le
attributes.text: e. "Commercial space" shall mean a space used or occupied for non-residential purposes pursuant to a valid commercial lease or other rental agreement and any space that can be so used pursuant to law or regulation.

attributes.label: f. "Commissioner" shall mean the head of the administering agency.
attributes.text: f. "Commissioner" shall mean the head of the administering agency.

attributes.label: g. "Landlord" shall mean any owner, lessor, sublessor or other person entitled to receive rent for the use or occupancy
attributes.text: g. "Landlord" shall mean any owner, lessor, sublessor or other person entitled to receive rent for the use or occupancy of any commercial premises, or an agent thereof.

attributes.label: h. "Pass-along" shall mean any taxes, sewer, water or utility fee, or other operating charges apportioned to a tenant in
attributes.text: h. "Pass-along" shall mean any taxes, sewer, water or utility fee, or other operating charges apportioned to a tenant in connection with the use or occupancy of any commercial space, but shall not include any charges that are individually metered to reflect the tenant's exclusive use of such space, including water, sewer and utility fees.

attributes.label: i. "Rent" shall mean any consideration, including but not limited to pass-alongs, received by the landlord in connection
attributes.text: i. "Rent" shall mean any consideration, including but not limited to pass-alongs, received by the landlord in connection with the use or occupancy of any commercial space.

attributes.label: j. "Services" shall mean those facilities which enhance the use of the commercial premises, including, but not limited t
attributes.text: j. "Services" shall mean those facilities which enhance the use of the commercial premises, including, but not limited to, repairs, maintenance, painting, heat, hot and cold water, utilities, elevator service, security devices and patrols, furnishings, storage, janitorial and landscaping services, refuse removal, insurance protection, parking spaces and facilities in common areas of the building or parcel in which the rental unit is located.

attributes.label: k. "Tenant" shall mean a tenant, subtenant, lessee, sublessee, or any other persons lawfully entitled to use or occupy a
attributes.text: k. "Tenant" shall mean a tenant, subtenant, lessee, sublessee, or any other persons lawfully entitled to use or occupy any commercial premises.

attributes.label: § 22-1503 Commercial rent guidelines board. a. There shall be a
attributes.text: § 22-1503 Commercial rent guidelines board. a. There shall be a

attributes.label: commercial rent guidelines board consisting of nine members appointed by the mayor as follows:
attributes.text: commercial rent guidelines board consisting of nine members appointed by the mayor as follows:

attributes.label: (1) One public member to serve as the chairperson of the board;
attributes.text: (1) One public member to serve as the chairperson of the board;

attributes.label: (2) Two members representing commercial tenants which are not chain businesses;
attributes.text: (2) Two members representing commercial tenants which are not chain businesses;

attributes.label: (3) Two members representing commercial landlords, at least one of whom shall be a landlord owning ten or fewer commerci
attributes.text: (3) Two members representing commercial landlords, at least one of whom shall be a landlord owning ten or fewer commercial spaces; and

attributes.label: (4) Four additional public members, each of whom has at least five years of experience in finance, economics, real prope
attributes.text: (4) Four additional public members, each of whom has at least five years of experience in finance, economics, real property management, community organizing, or community development, which shall not include commercial landlords or persons who are employed by or representing a business improvement district. No public member of the board may own or manage any commercial rental property affected by the board's orders or be an officer in any organization representing tenants or owners.

attributes.label: b. The members of the board, except the chairperson, shall serve staggered terms of two years. Four members of the board
attributes.text: b. The members of the board, except the chairperson, shall serve staggered terms of two years. Four members of the board originally appointed, comprising one member representing tenants, one member representing landlords and two public members, shall serve until January first, two thousand twenty-eight. The other members of the board originally appointed, excluding the chairperson, shall serve until January first, two thousand twenty-nine. Thereafter, all members shall serve two-year terms on the board until their successors have been appointed and qualified, except the chairperson, who shall serve at the pleasure of the mayor.

attributes.label: c. The mayor shall fill any vacancy that may occur in the same manner as the original appointment. A member of the board
attributes.text: c. The mayor shall fill any vacancy that may occur in the same manner as the original appointment. A member of the board, other than the chairperson, may only be removed by the mayor for cause after an opportunity to be heard in person or by counsel, in the member's defense, upon at least ten days written notice.

attributes.label: d. The chairperson shall be the chief administrative officer of the board and shall have the authority to employ, assign
attributes.text: d. The chairperson shall be the chief administrative officer of the board and shall have the authority to employ, assign and supervise the members of the board and enter into contracts for consultant services. The commissioner shall cooperate with the board and may assign personnel and perform such services in connection with the duties of the board as may reasonably be required by the chairperson.

attributes.label: e. The members of the board shall be compensated on a per diem basis for no more than fifty days per year at a rate to b
attributes.text: e. The members of the board shall be compensated on a per diem basis for no more than fifty days per year at a rate to be determined by the mayor, and the chairperson shall be compensated on a per diem basis for no more than one hundred days per year at a rate to be determined by the mayor.

attributes.label: f. The board shall establish initial guidelines for commercial rent adjustments by the first of July next succeeding app
attributes.text: f. The board shall establish initial guidelines for commercial rent adjustments by the first of July next succeeding appointment of the last member of the board. Thereafter, the board shall establish annual guidelines to be filed in accordance with subdivision g of this section. In determining whether to adjust rents for commercial spaces subject to the commercial rent stabilization provisions of this chapter, the board shall consider, among other things:

attributes.label: (1) The economic condition of the commercial real estate industry in the community board district, including such factor
attributes.text: (1) The economic condition of the commercial real estate industry in the community board district, including such factors as:

attributes.label: (i) commercial real estate taxes and sewer and water rates;
attributes.text: (i) commercial real estate taxes and sewer and water rates;

attributes.label: (ii) gross operating and maintenance costs, including but not limited to insurance rates, governmental fees, fuel and la
attributes.text: (ii) gross operating and maintenance costs, including but not limited to insurance rates, governmental fees, fuel and labor costs;

attributes.label: (iii) costs and availability of financing, including effective rates of interest; and
attributes.text: (iii) costs and availability of financing, including effective rates of interest; and

attributes.label: (iv) the overall supply of commercial spaces and overall vacancy rates;
attributes.text: (iv) the overall supply of commercial spaces and overall vacancy rates;

attributes.label: (2) Relevant data from the current and projected market values of
attributes.text: (2) Relevant data from the current and projected market values of

attributes.label: commercial rentals in the community board district;
attributes.text: commercial rentals in the community board district;

attributes.label: (3) The socioeconomic and demographic changes in each community board district based on the most recent available data,
attributes.text: (3) The socioeconomic and demographic changes in each community board district based on the most recent available data, including but not limited to changes in:

attributes.label: (i) the median income level;
attributes.text: (i) the median income level;

attributes.label: (ii) education;
attributes.text: (ii) education;

attributes.label: (iii) race;
attributes.text: (iii) race;

attributes.label: (iv) ethnicity; and
attributes.text: (iv) ethnicity; and

attributes.label: (v) home ownership; and
attributes.text: (v) home ownership; and

attributes.label: (4) Any other relevant data available to the board.
attributes.text: (4) Any other relevant data available to the board.

attributes.label: g. Not later than July first of each year, the board shall file with the city clerk its guidelines for the preceding cal
attributes.text: g. Not later than July first of each year, the board shall file with the city clerk its guidelines for the preceding calendar year, and shall accompany such findings with a statement of the maximum rate or rates of rent adjustment, if any, for all commercial spaces subject to the provisions of this chapter authorized for leases or other rental agreements commencing on the first of October next succeeding or within twelve months thereafter. Such guidelines and statement shall be published in the city record.

attributes.label: h. Prior to the annual adjustment of the level of rents provided for under subdivision f of this section, the board shal
attributes.text: h. Prior to the annual adjustment of the level of rents provided for under subdivision f of this section, the board shall hold at least two public hearings for the purpose of collecting information relating to all factors set forth in subdivision f of this section, and any other relevant information as may be necessary for establishing the annual adjustment guidelines. The board shall provide notice of the date, time and location and a summary of the subject matter of the public hearings, to be published in the city record daily for the period beginning eight days prior to the hearing date, and at least once in one or more newspapers of general circulation at least eight days immediately preceding such hearing date.

attributes.label: i. Maximum rates of rent adjustment shall not be established more than once annually for any commercial space subject to
attributes.text: i. Maximum rates of rent adjustment shall not be established more than once annually for any commercial space subject to the provisions of this

attributes.label: chapter. Once established, no such rate shall, within the one-year period, be adjusted by any surcharge, supplementary a
attributes.text: chapter. Once established, no such rate shall, within the one-year period, be adjusted by any surcharge, supplementary adjustment or other modification except as provided in section 22-1508 of this chapter.

attributes.label: j. The administering agency shall publish a form lease required to be used by landlords in establishing new tenancies af
attributes.text: j. The administering agency shall publish a form lease required to be used by landlords in establishing new tenancies after the effective date of this chapter.

attributes.label: § 22-1504 Stabilization provisions. a. Upon execution or renewal of a lease for commercial space, the annual rent charge
attributes.text: § 22-1504 Stabilization provisions. a. Upon execution or renewal of a lease for commercial space, the annual rent charged for the new lease term shall not exceed the initial legal regulated rent or legal regulated rent adjusted pursuant to section 22-1508 of this chapter until such time as a different legal regulated rent shall be authorized pursuant to guidelines adopted by the board established under section 22-1503 of this chapter. No landlord subject to the provisions of this chapter shall charge or collect any rent that exceeds the initial legal regulated rent or legal regulated rent adjusted pursuant to section 22-1508 of this chapter until such time as a different legal regulated rent has been authorized pursuant to guidelines adopted by the board. For any lease exceeding one year, the rent charged for any subsequent year shall not exceed the legal regulated rent as authorized pursuant to the most recent guidelines adopted by the board. If the rent charged for the first year of the new lease is less than the initial legal regulated rent or the legal regulated rent adjusted pursuant to section 22-1508 of this chapter, the rent charged for any subsequent year shall not exceed the first year's rent adjusted by the rate authorized pursuant to the most recent guidelines adopted by the board.

attributes.label: b. The initial regulated rent for a commercial space subject to the provisions of this chapter is the rent charged in th
attributes.text: b. The initial regulated rent for a commercial space subject to the provisions of this chapter is the rent charged in the lease or other rental agreement for such commercial space in effect sixty days prior to the effective date of this chapter.

attributes.label: c. The initial regulated rent for a commercial space subject to the provisions of this chapter, that is not subject to a
attributes.text: c. The initial regulated rent for a commercial space subject to the provisions of this chapter, that is not subject to a lease or other rental agreement on the effective date of this chapter, shall be the rent charged in the last lease or other rental agreement for such commercial space in effect prior to the effective date of this chapter. However, if a claim alleging commercial tenant harassment pursuant to

attributes.label: chapter nine of this title is brought against a landlord by the previous tenant as the means by which the vacancy was ef
attributes.text: chapter nine of this title is brought against a landlord by the previous tenant as the means by which the vacancy was effected and such previous tenant's claim is upheld by a court of competent jurisdiction, such landlord shall be liable for damages up to ten times the proposed new lease's monthly rent or fifty thousand dollars, whichever is greater, to be payable to the previous tenant, in addition to consequential damages and any other remedy available at law or equity.

attributes.label: d. Upon a finding of commercial tenant harassment pursuant to chapter nine of this title, the rent for the new tenant sh
attributes.text: d. Upon a finding of commercial tenant harassment pursuant to chapter nine of this title, the rent for the new tenant shall be no higher than the rent that could have been charged to the previous tenant pursuant to subdivision a of this section, retroactive to the beginning of the new tenancy. All other terms and conditions of the lease shall conform to the provisions of subdivision a of this section.

attributes.label: e. If a tenant is an at-will tenant, such tenant has the right to request a written lease agreement that shall conform t
attributes.text: e. If a tenant is an at-will tenant, such tenant has the right to request a written lease agreement that shall conform to the provisions of subdivision a of this section and be a monthly rent equivalent to the amount such tenant is paying at the time of such request. The landlord of an at-will tenant shall provide a written lease offer within ninety days of receiving such a request for a written lease. A landlord shall only be able to refuse to provide a written lease or evict an at-will tenant based on the provisions under section 22-1510 of this chapter, except for the provision set forth in paragraph two of such subdivision.

attributes.label: § 22-1505 Enforcement and procedures. a. Subject to the conditions and limitations of this section, any landlord who, up
attributes.text: § 22-1505 Enforcement and procedures. a. Subject to the conditions and limitations of this section, any landlord who, upon the complaint of a tenant, is found by the commissioner, after a reasonable opportunity to be heard, to have collected an overcharge above the rent authorized for a commercial space subject to the provisions of this chapter, is liable to such tenant for a penalty equal to three times the amount of such overcharge. If the landlord establishes, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the overcharge was not intentional, the penalty shall be the amount of the overcharge plus interest assessed from the initial date of such overcharge. After a complaint of rent overcharge has been filed and served on a landlord, the voluntary adjustment of the rent and/or the voluntary tender of a refund of rent overcharges shall not be considered by the commissioner as evidence that such overcharge was not willful.

attributes.label: b. The legal regulated rent for purposes of determining an overcharge is the rent indicated in the annual registration s
attributes.text: b. The legal regulated rent for purposes of determining an overcharge is the rent indicated in the annual registration statement filed and served upon the tenant six years prior to the most recent registration statement, or, if more recently filed, the initial registration statement plus, for each case, any subsequent lawful increases and adjustments. The commissioner, in investigating complaints of overcharge and in determining legal regulated rent, shall consider all available rent history which is reasonably necessary to make such determinations. As to complaints filed within ninety days of the initial registration of a commercial space, the legal regulated rent is deemed to be the rent charged on the date six years prior to the date of the initial registration of the commercial space or, if the commercial space was subject to this chapter for less than six years, the initial legal regulated rent plus, in each case, any lawful increases and adjustments. Where the rent charged on the date six years prior to the date of the initial registration of the commercial space cannot be established, such rent shall be established by the commissioner based on, among other things, the factors set forth in paragraph one of subdivision f of section 22-1503 of this chapter.

attributes.label: c. Complaints under this section may be filed with the commissioner at any time, however any recovery of overcharge pena
attributes.text: c. Complaints under this section may be filed with the commissioner at any time, however any recovery of overcharge penalties shall be limited to the six years preceding the complaint.

attributes.label: d. In addition to applicable penalties, a landlord found to have overcharged a tenant may be assessed the reasonable cos
attributes.text: d. In addition to applicable penalties, a landlord found to have overcharged a tenant may be assessed the reasonable costs and attorneys' fees of any necessary proceeding and interest from the initial date of the overcharge at the rate of interest payable on a judgment pursuant to section five thousand four of the civil practice law and rules.

attributes.label: e. A tenant may, upon the expiration of the period in which the landlord may institute a proceeding pursuant to article
attributes.text: e. A tenant may, upon the expiration of the period in which the landlord may institute a proceeding pursuant to article seventy-eight of the civil practice law and rules, file and enforce an order of the commissioner awarding penalties in the same manner as a judgment.

attributes.label: f. The commissioner shall promulgate all rules and regulations necessary for the implementation of this section.
attributes.text: f. The commissioner shall promulgate all rules and regulations necessary for the implementation of this section.

attributes.label: § 22-1506 Rent registration. a. Each landlord of a commercial space subject to the provisions of this chapter shall regi
attributes.text: § 22-1506 Rent registration. a. Each landlord of a commercial space subject to the provisions of this chapter shall register such space with the administering agency within one hundred twenty days of the effective date of this chapter and annually thereafter using forms prescribed by the commissioner and including copies of all leases and riders thereto. The information to be provided on such forms shall include the following:

attributes.label: (1) The name and address of the building or group of buildings or development in which such commercial space is located

attributes.text: (4) The rent for the commercial space charged on the registration date; and

attributes.text: (5) The square footage of each commercial space named pursuant to paragraph one of this subdivision.

attributes.text: b. The rental history shall include, if applicable, any overcharges, rent adjustments, the effective date of any new and collectible rents, and any tax benefits or financing programs that apply to the building. The administering agency shall inform the tenant of such commercial space of the registration and of the tenant's option to apply for an adjustment of the initial rent pursuant to section 22-1508 of this chapter within thirty days of such registration.

attributes.label: § 22-1507 Fees. a. The department of finance shall collect from the landlord of each commercial space registered pursuan
attributes.text: § 22-1507 Fees. a. The department of finance shall collect from the landlord of each commercial space registered pursuant to section 22-1506 of this chapter an annual fee in the amount of one hundred dollars for each commercial space subject to this chapter, in order to defray costs incurred in administering this chapter.

attributes.label: b. Failure to pay the fee imposed by subdivision a of this section shall constitute a charge due to the city. All such f
attributes.text: b. Failure to pay the fee imposed by subdivision a of this section shall constitute a charge due to the city. All such fees due to the city constitute a debt recoverable from the landlord and the city may commence an action or proceeding, file a lien upon the building or take any other lawful action for the recovery of such fees.

attributes.label: § 22-1508 Application for adjustment of initial rent. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, a tenant or l
attributes.text: § 22-1508 Application for adjustment of initial rent. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, a tenant or landlord may, within sixty days of receipt of the notice of registration pursuant to section 22-1506 of this chapter, file with the board an application for adjustment of the initial legal regulated rent for such commercial space. In the event of such an application, both the owner and the tenant shall be notified and given a chance to respond to the application within thirty days. The board may adjust such initial legal regulated rent upon a finding that the presence of extraordinary circumstances materially affecting the initial legal regulated rent has resulted in a rent which is substantially different from the rents generally prevailing in the same area for substantially similar commercial spaces.

e. If a tenant is an at-will tenant, such tenant has the right to request a written lease agreement that shall conform to the provisions of subdivision a of this section and be a monthly rent equivalent to the amount such tenant is paying at the time of such request. The landlord of an at-will tenant shall provide a written lease offer within ninety days of receiving such a request for a written lease. A landlord shall only be able to refuse to provide a written lease or evict an at-will tenant based on the provisions under section 22-1510 of this chapter, except for the provision set forth in paragraph two of such subdivision.

§ 22-1510 Rental guidelines. a. All leases of a commercial premises may be renewed at the option of a tenant who did not lose the right to renew a lease under the grounds described in subdivision d of this section. Such lease renewals shall be for a minimum term of ten years, provided however, that at the tenant's option, and with the written approval of the landlord, a lease of shorter or longer duration may be selected.
b. No period of lease extension required by this chapter shall extend beyond the landlord's lawful ability to rent the premises to the tenant, where such ability is limited by:
(1) the obligation to rent the premises to a third party pursuant to a bona fide lease entered into prior to the effective date of this chapter;
(2) the exercise by a third party of a bona fide option to rent the premises provided that such option was given prior to the effective date of this chapter; or
(3) any other lawful reason arising prior to such effective date.
c. A tenant shall lose the right of renewal and a landlord may refuse to renew a lease only on the following grounds:

(1) The tenant has persistently delayed rent payments without cause. For the purpose of this subdivision, "cause" is defined as the withholding of rental payments by the tenant due to the alleged violations of the rental agreement by the landlord. In order for the landlord to be excused from renewal on this ground, the landlord must have served the tenant at least three prior notices during the term of the lease for demand of payment within thirty days, and then show that such lessee has not paid within such thirty-day period. The landlord shall not serve such notice unless the rent payment was in arrears for a minimum of fifteen days;
(2) The tenant uses the commercial premises in a manner substantially different from that described in the lease;
(3) The tenant conducts or permits any form of illegal activity on the premises;
(4) The tenant has substantially breached any substantive obligation under the current lease and has failed to cure such breach within thirty days following written notice to cure by the landlord;

(5) Upon the termination of the current tenancy, the landlord intends, in good faith, to demolish or substantially reconstruct the premises or a substantial part thereof, or to carry out substantial work or construction on the commercial premises or substantial part thereof which they could not reasonably do without obtaining possession of the commercial premises. The landlord shall notify the tenant of their decision to reoccupy the commercial premises at least one year prior to the termination of the lease. In the event that the lessor fraudulently invokes this justification for a refusal to renew a commercial lease, the defrauded tenant may collect treble damages for any loss suffered as a result of such action;

(6) The current tenancy was created by the subletting of the property, whereby the prime tenant did not notify the landlord by certified mail of the subtenant's existence and did not obtain the written consent of the landlord. This ground is void if the landlord and tenant had agreed in the lease to allow subleasing rights without the consent of the landlord and all obligations of the prime tenant on the issue, were in compliance;

(7) It has been determined by the administering agency or by a civil court of competent jurisdiction that the tenant is a gross and persistent violator of New York city tax laws, of any license obligations related to the use of the premises or of any laws of the city of New York; or

(8) Upon the termination of the current tenancy, the landlord intends to occupy the retail premises in order to carry out its own business, which cannot be the same type of business that the current tenant is operating. The landlord shall notify the tenant of their decision to reoccupy the premises at least one hundred eighty days prior to the termination of the lease. In the event that the landlord fraudulently invokes this justification for a refusal to renew a commercial lease, the defrauded tenant may collect treble damages for any loss suffered as a result of such action.

§ 22-1511 Retaliation. No landlord shall in any way retaliate against any tenant for the tenant's assertion or exercise of any rights under this chapter. Any such retaliation may subject the landlord to a suit for actual and punitive damages, injunctive relief, and attorneys' fees.
§ 22-1512 Waiver. No provision in any lease, rental agreement, or agreement made in connection therewith which waives or diminishes any tenant's rights under this chapter is valid.
§ 22-1513 Inconsistency with other laws. If any provision of this
chapter is inconsistent with, in conflict with, or contrary to any other provisions of law, such provision of this chapter shall prevail over such other provision.

attributes.text: Omitted source layer: Fair Rent NYC counsel added a full Legislative findings and intent section before the operative bill text. The current Albany article begins with the operative chapter instead. This is a strong candidate to restore in a future city intro because it builds the public-purpose record and explains the policy logic in plain language.

Application trigger: Albany partly carries the prospective-trigger idea from the 2022 redlines, but changes it to leases and rental agreements that are renewed, renegotiated, or entered into on or after July 1, 2025. Treat this as partly adopted / needs review , not as a direct counsel-reviewed carry-forward.

Drafting error to fix: Intro 93 and the Fair Rent NYC counsel redline define a chain by establishments sharing a common owner or principal. The Albany text says common landlord or principal. That changes the meaning: unrelated small businesses with the same landlord could be swept into “chain business.”

Adopted from the 2022 redlines: Broad commercial-space coverage and removal of the old square-footage carveouts. This is a good example of Albany carrying the Fair Rent NYC counsel-reviewed architecture forward.

Omitted / changed source layer: The 2022 Fair Rent NYC redline introduced an “affected area” framework so the board could set geographically sensitive rent-adjustment policy, with areas no larger than NYC and no smaller than a community district. Albany instead hard-codes “community board district” in several places. This is a city-intro design choice to revisit.

Review point: The 2022 redline used an enactment-based sixty-day baseline. Albany’s “effective date” phrasing may be easier to game if the effective date comes later. Candidate city-level fix: restore the anti-gaming baseline.

Albany-only / review-needed lane: At-will tenant lease-request rights respond to a real field problem, but they were not part of the 2022 counsel-reviewed city redline package. Keep as a promising parts-library item, not an automatic city-bill transplant.

Major Albany-only addition: § 22-1510 creates a commercial-tenure / right-of-renewal lane: tenant renewal option, minimum ten-year term, and enumerated grounds for refusal to renew. This is the main legal-review zone for Takings / automatic-renewal concerns and should not be assumed to carry Fair Rent NYC counsel’s prior stamp of review.

State-specific additions: Retaliation, waiver, inconsistency, and severability language may be useful protections, but they are Albany additions beyond the 2022 city-redline package. For a new city intro, decide which are portable, which need counsel review, and which belong only in the state lane.
